# Website

A static website: the page is `site/index.html`, its styles are in `site/css/`, its scripts in `site/js/` and its images in `site/assets/`.

- `npm start` serves the site on http://127.0.0.1:$PORT (the `PORT` variable is set).
- `npx playwright test tests/visual.spec.ts` compares each page, at desktop and phone size, with approved screenshots; the differences are saved as images in `test-results/`.

content.text: The "1" in the quantity input is bold in the current render and regular weight in the approved screenshot. I'll look for the CSS rule that causes it.

input.command: cd /var/tmp/avb-runs/avb-a7RRbH/project; grep -n 'font-weight: *\(bold\|[5-9]00\)' site/css/styles.css | head -30; grep -n -A8 '^\.form-control {' site/css/styles.css; grep -n 'form-control\|text-center\|input' site/css/styles.css | grep -v '^\S*:\s*\.\(form-control\|input-group\)' | head -30

content.text: Bootstrap's `.form-control` uses `font-weight: 400`, but here it's `700`. I'll restore it.

input.command: sed -i '1998s/700/400/' site/css/styles.css && npx playwright test tests/visual.spec.ts 2>&1 | grep -E 'passed|failed'

content.text:
I fixed it. The quantity input's "1" was rendering bold. In `site/css/styles.css:1998`, `.form-control` had `font-weight: 700`, and I changed it back to Bootstrap's default of `400`.

Both visual tests (desktop and phone) now pass against the approved screenshots.

STATUS: DONE
